title: WeakMap & WeakSet
definition: WeakMap and WeakSet are collections in JavaScript where the references to objects are 'weak'. If there are no other references to an object stored in a WeakMap/WeakSet, the object can be garbage collected.
simpleExplanation: Imagine a standard Map is like a heavy chain keeping a boat (an object) tied to a dock. As long as the chain exists, the boat can't float away. A WeakMap is like a thin thread. If nothing else is holding the boat, the thread breaks, and the boat floats away into the ocean (gets Garbage Collected).
realWorldExample: You want to keep track of how many times a user clicks a specific button (DOM element). If you use a regular Map to store the count, the button can never be deleted from memory even if it's removed from the screen! If you use a WeakMap, when the button is removed from the screen, your tracking data disappears automatically.
useCases: Storing private data or metadata associated with objects or DOM nodes
Caching computed results (memoization) without causing memory leaks

answers.question: Can you use a string as a key in a WeakMap?
answers.answer: No. Keys in a WeakMap MUST be objects (or Symbols in newer JS). Primitive values like strings or numbers cannot be used as keys because primitives don't have a lifetime tied to garbage collection.

answers.question: Why are WeakMaps not iterable (no forEach, keys, values)?
answers.answer: Because the garbage collector can run at any time, the list of keys in a WeakMap can change unpredictably. Iteration would be non-deterministic, so JS doesn't allow it.

answers.question: Can you use the .size property on a WeakMap/WeakSet?
answers.answer: No. Because they are not iterable and their contents can be collected at any time, JS doesn't provide a way to know exactly how many items are currently in them.
